hook_text: More than eight billion people, and yet huge parts of the Earth have almost nobody. Where is everyone?
clip_script: A world map in a classroom in Newcastle. Red stickers crowd onto eastern China, India and Bangladesh, Java, Europe, the north-east of the United States, Nigeria and the River Nile. Blue stickers spread over the Sahara, Siberia, northern Canada, central Australia, the Amazon and Antarctica. About six in every ten people live in Asia. Most people live on fertile plains, along rivers and near coasts. Very few live where it is too cold, too dry, too wet or too steep.
visual_style: Whiteboard world map with red clusters and blue empty spaces, then icons for plains, rivers and coasts versus ice, sand, jungle and mountains.
mood: Big-picture and curious, like a world tour from above.
pacing: A quick sticker game, then a continent-by-continent tour and two lists of reasons.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and mark three crowded and three empty areas on a world map in your atlas.
